chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki al-Razi, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Burd al-Dinawari, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Khurasani, the servant of al-Ridha (peace be upon him), who said:

A man from the zanaqiqa (atheists) came to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) while a group was in his presence. Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'O man! What is your view -- if the claim were your claim, and reality were not as you say it is, would we and you not be equal, with what we have prayed, fasted, paid zakat, and acknowledged causing us no harm?' The man fell silent.

Then Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'And if the claim were our claim -- and it is our claim -- would you not be ruined while we are saved?' The man said: 'May God have mercy on you! Make me find how He is and where He is.' He said: 'Woe to you! What you have set upon is wrong. He is the One who gave place to where without a where, and gave manner to how without a how. He cannot be known through how-ness, nor through where-ness, nor can He be grasped by any sense, nor compared to anything.'

The man said: 'Then He is nothing, since He cannot be grasped by any sense from among the senses.' Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Woe to you! When your senses were incapable of grasping Him, you denied His Lordship. Whereas we, when our senses are incapable of grasping Him, become even more certain that He is our Lord -- unlike anything among things.'

The man said: 'Then tell me -- when did He begin to exist?' Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Tell me when He did not exist, and I will tell you when He began.' The man said: 'Then what is the proof of Him?' Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'When I look at my body, and am unable to increase or decrease it in its breadth and length, or to repel harm from it and draw benefit to it, I know that this structure has a Builder. So I affirm Him -- together with what I observe of the orbiting of the celestial sphere by His power, the forming of clouds, the routing of winds, the course of the sun and moon and stars, and other than that from the wondrous, evident signs. I know that for all this there is a Determiner and a Creator.'

key_terms.أَيَّنَ الْأَيْنَ بِلَا أَيْنٍ: He gave place to where without a where -- God is the originator of the very category of spatial location
key_terms.الرُّبُوبِيَّة: Rububiyya -- Lordship, Divine sovereignty and creatorship
key_terms.الزَّنَادِقَة: Zanaqiqa -- plural of zindiq; atheists or freethinkers who denied Islamic theology
key_terms.الْأَيْنُونِيَّة: Aynuniyya -- where-ness, the quality of having a location
key_terms.الْفَلَك: al-Falak -- the celestial sphere; refers to the observable astronomical order
key_terms.الْكَيْفُوفِيَّة: Kayfufiyya -- how-ness, the quality of having a mode or manner
key_terms.الْمُقَدِّر: Muqaddir -- the Determiner, the One who assigns measures and proportions
key_terms.الْمُنْشِئ: Munshi -- the Creator, the One who originates existence
key_terms.كَيَّفَ الْكَيْفَ بِلَا كَيْفٍ: He gave manner to how without a how -- God created the category of how-ness itself

ai.seo_question: What argument did Imam al-Ridha give to an atheist about God's existence and transcendence?
ai.summary: In this dialogue, Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s.) engages an atheist (zindiq) in a sophisticated theological exchange. The Imam begins with a pragmatic argument: if the atheists are right, believers and disbelievers are equally unaffected, but if the believers are right, the atheists face total ruin. He then addresses the epistemological challenge: God transcends the categories of 'how' and 'where' entirely, so the inability of the senses to perceive Him is not evidence against His existence but rather evidence of His absolute transcendence. Finally, the Imam presents the argument from design: the human body and the ordered cosmos demonstrate a Determiner and Creator behind all of creation.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on you

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ja’far Al Asady narrated to me, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Al Barmakky Al Qazy, from Al Husayn Bin Al Hassan Bin Burd Al Deynawary, from Muhammad Bin Ali, 
(It has been narrated) from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Al-Khurasany, a servant of Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> who said,

‘A man from the atheists came over to Abu Al-Hassanasws, and in hisasws presence was a group. So Abu Al-Hassanasws said: ‘O you man! What is your view if the word was your word (atheism), and it is not as what you are saying it to be, wouldn’t we and you all would be both equally right, and it would not harm us what we are praying Salāt, and our Fasting, and our (payment of) Zakāt, and our acknowledgement (of Allahazwj)?’. So the man was silent.

Then Abu Al-Hassanasws said: ‘And if it was so that the word was our word (Existence of Allahazwj), and it is our word, wouldn’t you be destroyed and we would be Saved?’ So he said, ‘May Allahazwj have Mercy on youasws! Help me find How Heazwj is and where Heazwj is?’ So heasws said: ‘Woe be unto you! That which goes to Himazwj is wrong. Heazwj is ‘where’ without a ‘where’, and ‘how’ without the ‘how’, so Heazwj cannot be recognised by the ‘how-ness’ nor by the ‘where-ness’, nor can Heazwj be attained by the feelings, nor can Heazwj be compared with anything’.

So the man said, ‘So He<sup>azwj</sup> is ‘nothing’ when He<sup>azwj</sup> cannot be realised by the feelings from the senses’. So Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Woe be unto you! Your senses are unable to realise Him<sup>azwj</sup>, so you are denying His<sup>azwj</sup> Lordship, and us<sup>asws</sup>, when our senses are unable to realise realise Him<sup>azwj</sup>, we are even more convinced that He<sup>azwj</sup> is our Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, as a different thing from the things’.

The man said, ‘So inform me, when was He<sup>azwj</sup> (from)?’ Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Inform me<sup>asws</sup>, when He<sup>azwj</sup> wasn’t and I<sup>asws</sup> will inform you when He<sup>azwj</sup> was’. The man said, ‘So what is the evidence upon it?’ So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup>, when I<sup>asws</sup> look at my<sup>asws</sup> body, and am not enabled upon increasing it, nor reducing it in the width, and the length, and repulsing the abhorrence from it and flowing the benefits to it, I<sup>asws</sup> know that for this construction, there is a Builder. So I<sup>asws</sup> acknowledge with it what I<sup>asws</sup> see from the orbiting of the planets by His<sup>azwj</sup> Power, and the growth of the clouds, and the interchanging of the winds, and the flowing of the sun and the moon and the stars, and other than that from the wondrous clear signs, I<sup>asws</sup> know that for this is Determiner and a Builder’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Ja‘far al-Asadi has narrated from Muhammad ibn Esma‘il al-Barmaki al-Razi from al-Husayn ibn al-Hassan ibn Bard al-Daynuri from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah al-Khurasani the an employee of Imam al-Rida (a.s.) who has said the following.

“An atheist man came to Imam abu al-Hassan (a.s.) while group of people was present there. The Imam (a.s.) said to him, “Consider, if what you say would be true which is not true, in such case, we all will be equal. Our fasting, prayers, giving charity and belief will not harm us.” The man remained quite.

The Imam then said, “If what we say would be true, which, in fact, is true then you will be the one facing your destruction and we will be saved.” The man then said, “Please help me learn where is He and how is He?” The Imam then said, “What is the matter with you? What you say is not right. He is the ‘where’ of ‘where’ but without ‘where’. He is the ‘how’ of ‘how’ without ‘how’. He can not be defined with ‘how’ and ‘where’ and can not be comprehended with the senses or compared with anything.”
The man then asked, “Tell me then when was He?” The Imam replied, “You tell me, when He was not there so that I would tell when He was there?”

The man then asked, “What is the proof for His existence?” The Imam said, “When I look at my body I find that I can not do any addition or alteration to it such as width and breadth or remove its sufferings and attract all its interests. I then come to understand that for this establishment there must be a founder and then I acknowledge His existence. Besides, I see all the orbiting planets and stars, the creation of the clouds and driving of the winds, the paths of the sun, the moon, the stars and other things of the marvelous clear signs I come to believe that there is One who has designed and created all such wonderful things”
